policy: Pending means not yet reviewed, not unclear/no. Corpus membership and historical coding are unchanged. Complete reviews use coding_amendment_2026-09-23.md and metric-specific evidence records; completion is not independent validation or successful recomputation.

notes: reviews/04.json records the twelve-page arXiv v5 including both appendices, five result groups, all six judgments and pinned artifact checks; supersedes the partial batch_02_05.md entry.

papers.title: Enhancing the Transferability of Adversarial Attacks through Variance Tuning
notes: reviews/05.json covers arXiv v3, separately retrieved CVF supplement, seven result groups and six judgments; supersedes the partial batch_02_05.md entry.

papers.title: PRADA: Protecting Against DNN Model Stealing Attacks
notes: reviews/06.json completes the seventeen-page main/appendix review, fifteen outcome/population-specific groups, all six judgments and pinned public artifact inspection.
All-seed transfer population supports no source-success conditioning as reported; target-clean preselection and actual evaluator implementation remain unresolved.
Held-out target test accuracies cannot bound attacker-seed transfer rates. Public defense wrapper is not a verified original transfer recomputation bundle.

papers.title: Improving Adversarial Robustness via Promoting Ensemble Diversity
notes: reviews/07.json covers all thirteen arXiv pages, the three-page PMLR supplement, eight transfer groups and all six judgments; supersedes the partial batch_01_06_10.md entry.
Separate clean errors are reported for all transfer members, but Figure 3 population alignment and conditioning are unresolved; targeted outcomes are not unconditional error rates.

Downloaded and structurally inspected the released standard ADP checkpoint. Available iterative evaluator scores the averaged ensemble, not Figure 3 member transfer; no runtime replication or numerical bound added.

papers.title: Do Adversarially Robust ImageNet Models Transfer Better?
notes: reviews/08.json completes the 31-page arXiv and separate 16-page NeurIPS supplement review. All located transfer experiments concern transfer learning, not cross-model attacked inputs.
Retained in the frozen corpus with all six fields unclear for non-applicability, not missing reporting. No numerical bounds or recomputability failure inferred.
Original GitHub URL is unavailable on the audit date; author Hugging Face model collection and a representative pinned checkpoint HEAD are accessible. No runtime executed.

papers.title: Why Do Adversarial Attacks Transfer? Explaining Transferability of Evasion and Poisoning Attacks
notes: reviews/09.json completes all nineteen arXiv pages, six result groups and six judgments; supersedes the partial batch_01_06_10.md entry.
Clean-target rows accompany evasion matrices, but denominator and malware operating-point alignment remain unresolved. Poisoning is not silently treated as fixed-predictor evasion.
Pinned SecML tutorial and attack implementation cite the paper; synthetic tutorial training is not a verified original experiment bundle. No numerical bound or runtime replication added.

papers.title: Is Robustness the Cost of Accuracy? - A Comprehensive Study on the Robustness of 18 Deep Image Classification Models
notes: reviews/10.json covers the full paper and embedded supplement, eight transfer groups and all six judgments.
Released evaluator explicitly excludes target-clean mistakes and retains source failures; correspondence to every published panel remains unresolved.
Original TensorFlow 1.8 FGSM/model classes executed for one same-size pair; predictions and qualified comparison archived in recomputation/su18_original. Not a full published-table replication.

papers.title: Adversarial Attack and Defense on Graph Data: A Survey
notes: reviews/11.json covers the twenty-page arXiv v4 including both appendices. Located tables and metrics summarize prior work, not original empirical transfer results.
Retained with non-applicability reasons for all six fields; accessible author bibliography is not counted as a transfer recomputability success or failure.

papers.title: On Evaluating Adversarial Robustness of Large Vision-Language Models
notes: reviews/12.json covers all 28 arXiv v2 pages including Appendices A-C; one pure-transfer group (Table 2 MF-it/MF-ii), with query-based MF-tt results excluded.

Outcome is mean CLIP similarity to a target caption; clean-image baselines are reported per model, but clean-correct and source-success events are undefined, so fields 1-4 are unclear for task mapping. Explicit L-infinity epsilon 8/255.
Pinned AttackVLM code inspected; Google Drive data not verified and Table 2 sample unidentified. No bound: continuous non-classification outcome.

papers.title: Skip Connections Matter: On the Transferability of Adversarial Examples Generated with ResNets
notes: reviews/13.json covers all fifteen arXiv pages including Appendices A-C; three groups (unsecured, secured, ablations) and six judgments.

5,000 images filtered on all eight source models only; this covers targets that are also sources but not the other targets, so field 2 stays unclear. Success-rate denominator not defined relative to source success.

Later author repository with 5,000-image subset and public torchvision weights is a recomputation candidate; released evaluator scores all adversarial images and uses step epsilon/steps unlike the stated alpha=2. Not executed.

papers.title: DPATCH: An Adversarial Patch Attack on Object Detectors
notes: reviews/14.json covers all eight arXiv v4 pages (no supplement); two transfer groups: cross-detector (Tables 1-2) and cross-dataset (Table 5).

Detection mAP with per-detector no-patch baselines; clean-correct and source-success events are undefined for dataset-level mAP. Field 5 is an explicit patch-area threat model without an L2/L-infinity radius.
Unlinked YOLO-only repository (veralauee/DPatch) inspected; no Faster R-CNN path, so neither transfer direction is covered. No bound: non-classification outcome.

papers.title: AdvHat: Real-World Adversarial Attack on ArcFace Face ID System
notes: reviews/15.json covers all nine arXiv v1 pages; one transfer scope (Figure 8, three InsightFace models, 10 volunteers). ICPR version not inspected.

The paper explicitly reports similarity differences instead of thresholded success rates, so fields 1-4 are unclear for task mapping; field 5 is an explicit physical-sticker threat model without an L2/L-infinity radius.
Linked MIT code inspected; volunteer photographs needed for Figure 8 are not released. No bound: continuous similarity outcome.

papers.title: Feature Importance-aware Transferable Adversarial Attacks
notes: reviews/16.json covers arXiv v3, the CVF ICCV version (Table 1 NRDM/FDA baseline rows differ between versions) and the twelve-page CVF supplement; two groups (normal and defense targets).
Success rate, clean accuracy and conditioning are not defined in the paper; explicit L-infinity epsilon 16 for all experiments. Table 3 prints identical PIM and PITIDIM rows.
Linked release includes the 1,000 images and evaluator; its logged success rate is a prediction-change rate over all 1,000 images. Recomputation candidate; checkpoints and execution unverified.

papers.title: Parametric Noise Injection: Trainable Randomness to Improve Deep Neural Network Robustness Against Adversarial Attack
notes: reviews/17.json covers arXiv v1, the CVF CVPR version (differences confined to white-box tables) and the four-page CVF supplement; two transfer groups (Table 5 ResNet-18 A/B; supplement AlexNet substitute).

Supplement Table 2 prints target and substitute clean accuracies separately, but the attacked population, attack and budget are unstated; ResNet-18 clean accuracies are missing and PNI targets are stochastic at inference.
Linked repository covers ResNet-20 PNI training/evaluation only; no transfer configuration. No bound extracted.

papers.title: A Survey on Safety-Critical Driving Scenario Generation—A Methodological Perspective
notes: reviews/18.json covers all eighteen arXiv v6 pages; a methodological survey of driving-scenario generation with no original attack or transfer experiment.
Retained with non-applicability reasons for all six fields; scenario 'transferability' is discussed only conceptually.

papers.title: Improving Black-box Adversarial Attacks with a Transfer-based Prior
notes: reviews/19.json covers all 23 arXiv v3 pages including Appendices A-D. All attacks are score-based queries to the target with a surrogate gradient prior; no zero-query transfer rate is reported.
Retained with non-applicability reasons; the boundary between transfer-prior query attacks and transfer evaluation is documented for the independent recoder.

papers.title: Enhancing Adversarial Example Transferability With an Intermediate Level Attack
notes: reviews/20.json covers all twenty arXiv v3 pages including Appendices A-H (v3 notes corrected normalization); four groups: CIFAR-10 full test set, ImageNet 50k torchvision, Table 1 5k ImageNet, Appendix G subset.

CIFAR-10 and 50k-ImageNet groups explicitly evaluate all inputs and all adversarial examples (fields 2/3 no); Table 1 and Appendix G populations are unresolved. CIFAR clean accuracies are reported for all four models; the ImageNet torchvision radius is unstated.

Official release logs clean and attacked accuracy per batch, with CIFAR-10 checkpoints on Drive: strong recomputation and bounds candidate, not yet executed. CIFAR bound extraction deferred to the corpus-wide pass.

papers.title: Admix: Enhancing the Transferability of Adversarial Attacks
notes: reviews/21.json covers the ten-page arXiv v3 and the identical CVF ICCV version (no supplement); three groups: single source, ensemble to adversarially trained targets, advanced defenses.
Success rate is defined as target misclassification without a population rule, so fields 2/3 are unclear, consistent with rank 5; explicit L-infinity epsilon 16 throughout.
Released simple_eval.py divides ground-truth misclassification counts by 1,000 without filtering; recomputation candidate with ranks 4-5. Drive data/models unverified.

papers.title: Adversarial Examples that Fool both Computer Vision and Time-Limited Humans
notes: reviews/22.json covers all 22 arXiv v3 pages and the fourteen-page full supplemental PDF from the goo.gl Drive link (tables match); groups: held-out model transfer and human-observer transfer.

Appendix D explicitly retains only adversarial images that fooled all 10 ensemble models (7/10 for the false condition), so field 3 is yes for all scopes. Table Supp.2 reports separate top-1 accuracy for all 12 models (field 1 yes).
No code or custom retina-layer checkpoints released. No bound: source-success conditioned, targeted coarse-class outcome.

papers.title: Frequency Domain Model Augmentation for Adversarial Attack
notes: reviews/23.json covers all 22 arXiv pages including supplementary Sections A-D; three groups (normal targets, defenses single-source, defenses ensemble-source).

Success rate is not formally defined and no clean accuracy is reported; explicit L-infinity epsilon 16 in all experiments. README RS 'skip=100' setting is inconsistent with the published RS resolution; unresolved.

Pinned official release (code plus 1,000 images; third-party converted weights) was executed historically with archived per-example predictions; checkpoint hashes and a manifest still need verification before field 6 can be yes.

papers.title: On the Robustness of Vision Transformers to Adversarial Examples
notes: reviews/24.json covers all 25 arXiv v2 pages including supplemental Sections A-G; groups: pairwise transfer (Table 2, Tables 10-12) and adaptive black-box transfer (Figure 3).

Pairwise transfer explicitly uses m = 1,000 jointly clean-correct examples (field 2 yes for that scope) and Eq. 3 retains source failures (field 3 no); the adaptive scope is unresolved, so both paper-level fields are unclear with preserved scope evidence.
CIFAR-10 checkpoints and attack code are released (Drive, unverified); the pairwise study is not packaged. No bound: the jointly clean cohort already has zero baseline error.

papers.title: NATTACK: Learning the Distributions of Adversarial Examples for an Improved Black-Box Attack on Deep Neural Networks
notes: reviews/25.json covers all thirteen arXiv v3 pages including supplementary pages; one transfer scope (Figure 2 BPDA/NATTACK confusion tables across CIFAR-10 defenses).

Section 3.3 explicitly transfers only source-correct, source-successful images (field 3 yes); clean accuracy is reported for every model (field 1 yes). Printed two-decimal rates are inconsistent with the stated 1,000-image denominator.
Release confusion.py only plots hard-coded values, transposed relative to the published figure; no transfer evaluator. No bound: source-success conditioned.

papers.title: Adversarial vulnerability for any classifier

notes: reviews/27.json covers all fifteen arXiv v2 pages including Appendices A-D; results concern model-extraction fidelity and query complexity, with no adversarial transfer evaluation.

papers.title: SparseFool: A Few Pixels Make a Big Difference
notes: reviews/28.json covers all fourteen arXiv v4 pages including supplementary Sections A-D; one transfer scope (Table 3, three ImageNet models, 4,000 images).

The fooling rate is formally defined over all of D as prediction change from each model's clean prediction, so fields 2/3 are explicit no. Clean accuracy is reported for all transfer models; field 5 is an explicit sparse attack without an L2/L-infinity radius.
Attack code is released with public torchvision weights; the 4,000-image sample and transfer evaluator are not. No bound: prediction-change outcome.

papers.title: Exploring Adversarial Examples in Malware Detection
notes: reviews/29.json covers all seven arXiv v3 pages; one transfer scope (EMBER and Full MalConv in both directions, Section V.C).
Transfer is explicitly evaluated only on source-evading samples whose originals the target classifies correctly (fields 2 and 3 yes); result stated as at most 2/400 per experiment.
Full model and data are proprietary; no release located. No bound: conditioned population.

papers.title: How Robust is Google's Bard to Adversarial Image Attacks?
notes: reviews/30.json covers all thirteen arXiv v2 pages; four scopes: Bard description, 20-image surrogate ablation, other commercial MLLMs, and Bard filter evasion.

The 100-image description scopes evaluate all images with same-image no-attack baselines (field 2 no for those scopes). Every rate is an integer percentage of a stated 100- or 20-image set, uniquely reconstructable (field 4 yes, reconstruction mode).
Release includes images and 200 adversarial examples but no per-example judgments; hosted targets are not reproducible. The same-image baseline analog is recorded but not added to bounds.

papers.title: Feature Space Perturbations Yield More Transferable Adversarial Examples
notes: reviews/31.json records six evidence-supported judgments, main/supplement coverage, four metric groups and artifact/bounds checks under the dated retrospective amendment.
Complete denotes documented non-blind evidence review, not artifact sufficiency, numerical replication or independent agreement.
Mixed explicit source conditioning must not be counted as absent denominator reporting. No new numerical bounds extracted.

papers.title: Patch-wise Attack for Fooling Deep Neural Network
notes: reviews/32.json covers all 21 arXiv v3 pages including appendix Tables 5-13; three groups (normal, ensemble-adversarially-trained and feature-denoising targets).

Feature-denoising target rates explicitly subtract the target's clean misclassification ratio, an explicit clean-error adjustment rather than a clean-correct denominator, so field 2 stays unclear while the evidence is preserved. Explicit L-infinity epsilon 16.
Release evaluates one target over 1,000 images without FD code; recomputation candidate.
